correctness.rationale: On \(\ell^1\) the column-sum norm formula is exact, including boundary columns and coefficient cancellation within the difference before taking absolute values. The binomial adjacent-mass ratio yields \(\sigma_n^2d_{n,k}\to |u|\varphi(u)\) locally, and a global Gaussian envelope plus total variation \(O(1/\sigma_n)\). For \(\alpha>1\) the singular lattice kernel is summable, yielding \(\zeta(\alpha)\); at \(\alpha=1\) the near-diagonal harmonic mass contributes precisely \(\log\sigma_n/\\(\log n\)\to1/2\), with far terms negligible. Outer columns are exponentially small or O(n^-1/2), and off-center columns vanish by the Gaussian envelope. The maximizing Gaussian derivative \(|u|\varphi(u)\) has value \(1/\sqrt{2\pi e}\) at exactly ±1. A standalone exact-rational finite-matrix test plus supplementary diagnostics passed 87 assertions. Numerical evidence is not used as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Arnold (arXiv:2610.00271v1, Example 3.2 and Section 7) provides the original weighted-shift model and general binomial lazy-averaging setting, but not the critical/supercritical sharp difference limits. The directly comparable full published-finding corpus research text explicitly assumes \(0<\alpha<1\) and uses a locally integrable fractional Gaussian kernel; its theorem and all quantified conclusions exclude \(\alpha\ge1\). The independent reflexive-space result assumes \(0<\alpha<1/p\), also excluding the claimed domain. The binomial-gradient/harmonic/zeta endpoint formulas are not logical consequences of those theorems without an additional singular-kernel boundary analysis, provided here. value.rationale: The formerly unresolved boundary \(\alpha=1\) is the natural singular-integrability cutoff in the exact subcritical Gaussian asymptotic for the same operator. The theorem identifies a new logarithmic-to-polynomial power-regularity transition, sharp delta-dependent constants, the zeta function appearing from a discrete boundary layer, and the location of extremizing columns.
